text.p: Israeli dollar-linked bonds rose sharply in an otherwise quiet market on Wednesday after the U.S. currency reached a 34-month high against the mark, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): -0.04 pct to 102.78
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.01 pct to 101.85.
Volume was a moderate 132 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds continue to rise. Sophisticated investors are focusing now on short- and medium-term bonds, but the Bank of Israel has stopped issuing new bonds and prices are rising," said one trader.
"Yields on inflation-linked bonds are already at 4.1 percent and they will continue to decline to 3.8-3.9 percent," he said.
Unlinked bonds fell for the second day running.

"The sharp rise of the dollar might accelerate inflation and the interest rate will remain unchanged. This will make these bonds less attractive," explained Yigal Mizrahi, chief analyst at Nesuah Trading and Investments.
Traders noted that the Makams, which are also unlinked, closed almost unchanged with turnover falling to only 35 million shekels.

Today's main gainers were dollar-linked bonds, which surged broadly following the dollar's rally in overseas markets. In the local forex market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3420 shekels against 3.3310 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
